architectural_finding_critical.title: Task spec V6.2 presumed a multi-channel scheme that does not exist in code — single private-branch.{id} channel is the design SSOT
architectural_finding_critical.task_spec_claim: Task spec V6.2 says verify `kds.branch.{id}` and `pos.shortcuts.branch.{id}` are keyed appropriately so cross-pollution doesn't happen.
architectural_finding_critical.actual_implementation: The codebase uses a SINGLE `private-branch.{branchId}` channel for ALL real-time events (KDS, POS, OSS, kiosk all subscribe to the same channel and filter client-side by `broadcastAs` event name). Channel name strings `kds.branch.{id}` and `pos.shortcuts.branch.{id}` DO NOT EXIST in the codebase.
evidence_files: routes/channels.php:41-62 — only TWO channel authz callbacks: `App.Models.User.{id}` (Sanctum user channel, default Laravel) + `branch.{branchId}` (the unified per-branch private channel)

resources/js/components/admin/pos/PosComponent.vue:2630-2680 — POS subscribes to `branch.{id}` and listens for events {OrderCreated, OrderStatusChanged, OrderPaidAtCounter, ItemAvailabilityChanged, CatalogChanged}

resources/js/components/admin/kitchenDisplaySystem/KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue:1848-1875 — KDS subscribes to the SAME `branch.{id}` channel and listens for {OrderStatusChanged, OrderCreated, OrderPaidAtCounter, ItemAvailabilityChanged, OrderTableChanged}
architectural_finding_critical.why_this_is_safe: Cross-pollution between KDS and POS does NOT happen at the channel layer because they share the channel intentionally. Pollution-prevention is achieved at the EVENT-NAME layer (`broadcastAs`) AND at the per-component listener-binding layer: each surface explicitly opts in to only the events it cares about (KDS does NOT bind `CatalogChanged`; POS does NOT bind `OrderTableChanged`). The architecture is sound and parsimonious — adding per-surface channels would require N×branches=N more `Broadcast::channel()` authz callbacks for ZERO behavioral gain. This is by design.
architectural_finding_critical.remediation_needed: NONE on the code side. Task spec language should be reworded for future audits: 'Verify each broadcast event-name (`OrderStatusChanged`, `OrderCreated`, etc.) is routed to the appropriate per-surface listener via the shared private-branch channel' is the accurate framing.

V6.2.cross_pollution_protection_mechanism: PER-EVENT-NAME OPT-IN at the component layer. Each component invokes `onEvents(branchId, [{ broadcastAs: 'EventName', handler: fn }, ...])` which calls `channel.listen(`.${broadcastAs}`, rawHandler)` — Pusher delivers ALL events on the channel to all subscribers, but Echo's `.listen(`.EventName`, ...)` API filters by event name before invoking the handler. Result: KDS code never executes a `CatalogChanged` handler because KDS does not bind it. POS code never executes an `OrderTableChanged` handler because POS does not bind it. Cross-pollution is structurally impossible.
V6.2.branch_isolation_via_authz_callback: routes/channels.php:41-62 enforces branch_id isolation at the AUTHORIZATION layer. A staff user with branch_id=3 cannot subscribe to `private-branch.5` because the callback returns false. A kiosk token can only subscribe to its own machine's branch (token-name check, immune to Sanctum wildcard tokenCan). Admin/Tenant Admin role check (post-R3 T-3.2.2 Sec F-SEC-W6-01/02 heal) closes the Guest-Echo-Bypass latent path — customers/guests with branch_id=0 cannot subscribe to arbitrary branches.
V6.2.double_subscribe_protection: KitchenDisplaySystemComponent.vue:1846 — `this.unsubscribeEcho()` called BEFORE every `subscribeEcho()` (AUDIT-P51-BUG2 fix). Prevents duplicate listener leak on re-mount/HMR. PosComponent.vue:2085+2135 has equivalent `_unsubscribeEcho()` before `_subscribeEcho()` pattern.

V6.4.scenario: User A logs in to POS in tab A. User A logs out. Token should be revoked. Reopen tab A → redirected to /login (no stale state).
V6.4.verdict: PASS_BY_STATIC_PROOF — server-side delete + client-side persistent state mutation both correct, with one DOCUMENTED CAVEAT

evidence_lines: Line 147-166 — `public function logout(Request $request): JsonResponse`
Line 149-150 — `$user = $request->user(); $current = $user?->currentAccessToken();`
Line 152-153 — `if ($current instanceof PersonalAccessToken) { $current->delete(); }` — DELETE the row from personal_access_tokens table. The row is gone server-side immediately.
Line 154-160 — Defensive fallback if `currentAccessToken()` returned a TransientToken (cookie auth path): re-find by bearer, verify tokenable identity (prevent cross-user delete), then delete.
Line 163-165 — Returns 200 + logout_success message.
server_side_token_delete.verdict_reasoning: Once `delete()` returns, ANY subsequent request bearing the same token will fail Sanctum's `auth:sanctum` middleware (PersonalAccessToken::findToken() returns null → 401 Unauthenticated). Cannot be replayed.

evidence_lines: Line 73-82 — `logout` Vuex action: `axios.post('auth/logout').then((res) => { context.commit('authLogout'); resolve(res); })` — calls server logout, THEN commits client-side mutation.

Line 157-166 — `authLogout` mutation: sets `state.authStatus = false; state.authToken = null; state.authBranchId = ''; state.authInfo = {}; state.authMenu = []; state.authPermission = {}; ...` — clears all auth fields.

vuex_persistedstate_propagation.evidence: createPersistedState plugin paths includes `auth`. The plugin subscribes to ALL store mutations and writes the matched paths back to localStorage SYNCHRONOUSLY in the mutation handler. When `authLogout` mutation runs, `state.auth = { authToken: null, ... }` is immediately reflected in `localStorage.vuex`. Combined with axios .then() ordering (server delete first, mutation second), the cleanup is atomic from the user's perspective.
vuex_persistedstate_propagation.verdict_reasoning: After logout completes (POST resolved), localStorage.vuex.auth.authToken=null is written before any further user action is possible (Promise resolution is sync within the JS event loop turn). Reopen tab A → SPA boots, auth.authToken=null in store, navigation guard sees unauthenticated state → redirect to /login. Sanctum 401 fallback also exists for any race: resources/js/app.js:174 — `store.dispatch('logout').catch(() => {})` is triggered on 401 from any API call, providing defense-in-depth.

documented_caveat.description: The Vuex axios.post('auth/logout').then() pattern has a window between (a) HTTP request completion and (b) `authLogout` mutation commit. If the user closes the tab DURING the in-flight POST (server already received and deleted the token, but Promise has not resolved client-side), the client never commits `authLogout` — but this is harmless because: (1) the server has already deleted the token (no replay possible), (2) on next boot the SPA will attempt any authenticated request, receive 401, and the global 401 interceptor (app.js:174) will dispatch the logout action, which will re-commit authLogout and clear localStorage. Net effect: the user lands on /login eventually. Not a security issue, just a minor UX inelegance (e.g. SPA boots briefly showing 'logged in' chrome before 401 fires).
documented_caveat.remediation_priority: V1.0.2 backlog at most. Optional fix: clear localStorage synchronously BEFORE the axios.post call. Trade-off: if the POST fails (offline), the user is locally logged out but the server still holds a valid token. Current order is the safer choice for the security model.

kiosk_token_logout_separate_path.evidence: Separate logout endpoint POST /api/auth/kiosk-logout (routes/api.php:197). Kiosk token-name='kiosk-token' is mint-revoked at re-login (LoginController:109 — 'auth_token' name → tokens()->where('name', 'auth_token')->delete()). Token sprawl mitigation (Wave 5D Z6-01). Each kiosk machine login revokes prior tokens for the same user — confirms task spec assumption.

broadcast_channel_subscription_after_log.evidence: Once token is deleted, the next pusher:subscription_error (token rejected by /api/broadcasting/auth) triggers the F-12 handler in bootstrap.js:359-372 — `_bindSubscriptionErrorHandler` calls `window._refreshEchoAuth()` (tries to re-read localStorage token, which is now null → re-auth fails again) AND `wsService.handleSubscriptionError()` (sliding-window counter promotes to SESSION_INVALID after 3 failures in 60s). Final state: Echo gives up subscribing, polling fallback continues — no stale broadcast event delivery to a logged-out tab is possible because the channel-auth would reject the (now-deleted) token.
